thread:
maya: Posted a fresh Dark Mode round for Console. Focusing on: global palette, syntax theme for code blocks, and chart color set (esp multi-series). Mock: https://figma.redwood/dark-theme-v3

dinesh: Nice! First impression: overall tones feel warmer. Card elevation looks fine but the divider lines are barely visible on my laptop. Maybe bump divider to rgba(255,255,255,0.06).

tara: Agree on divider. Also, the inline token highlights (like variable names) lose definition against the primary teal. We should avoid using brand teal for both UI accents and code token highlights.

maya: Good call. I separated 'brand' vs 'semantic' greens in this pass. Brand: #26b89a. Semantic success: #18a67f (a bit deeper). Code token preview I set to #9fe6c9 which might be too pale.

kevin: For syntax theme I prototyped 'Dracula-adj' -> purple keywords, warm strings, cyan numbers. Example snippet in mock. Strings were #f39c12 in that prototype.

maya: I like purple keywords. But watch contrast for strings on code-bg (#0b0d0f). a11y-bot will flag low contrast.

a11y-bot: Contrast checks:
- body text (#e8f0f2) on page-bg (#07090b): 15.8:1 ✅
- card text (#dde6ea) on card-bg (#0c0f11): 12.6:1 ✅
- divider (rgba white 0.04) on card-bg: 2.5:1 ⚠️ (below AA)
- code-string (#f39c12) on code-bg (#081015): 3.2:1 ⚠️ (below AA)
- primary (#26b89a) on card-bg: 4.4:1 ✅

maya: Thanks. I'll increase divider to 0.06 and nudge string to #f6b84a.

dinesh: Chart colors: we need at least 8 for stacked area and line combos. Also, make sure colors still distinguishable if someone prints in grayscale (or uses colorblind palette). What about adding different stroke styles (dashed/dotted) for lines in addition to color?

tara: Love stroke styles + markers for accessibility. For colorblind friendliness, add a palette variant (cb-safe):
- #4d79ff (blue)
- #ff8a00 (orange)
- #86c166 (olive)
- #d15c9f (magenta)
- #9fb3ff (light blue)
- #ffcc66 (gold)
- #a6a6a6 (neutral gray)
- #c18cff (lavender)

kevin: Can we avoid bright neon greens; they clash with success semantic and primary. Also avoid pure red for errors in charts — it's alarming next to alerts.

maya: Agreed. For chart palette 'stable' I propose:
- Blue: #4d79ff
- Orange: #f39c12
- Mint: #57c2a6
- Magenta: #d46b9b
- Lavender: #b7aaff
- Soft Yellow: #ffd88a
- Slate Gray: #98a0a8
- Teal Accent: #2aa184

dinesh: That teal accent is too close to brand. Suggest shift teal accent slightly more blue: #2aa1b8

a11y-bot: Color distance checks (simulating common CVD): mint (#57c2a6) vs teal accent (#2aa1b8) -> pass distance threshold for protanopia and deuteranopia. Contrast of soft yellow (#ffd88a) on page-bg (#07090b): 7.1:1 ✅

tara: UX copy nit: In Preferences, change "Dark"/"Light" toggle labels to "Dark (recommended for low-light)" and "Light (recommended for bright environments)" — adds quick context.

kevin: Small CSS implementation note: please expose theme tokens in JS as kebab-case and camelCase variants so both CSS-in-JS and legacy styles can consume easily.

maya: Action items:
- maya: update figma with divider 0.06, string color #f6b84a, chart palette with teal->blue shift; upload new prototype by tomorrow noon
- dinesh: add stroke/marker variants for chart component and wire to legend toggles
- kevin: add theme token mapping for frontend and leave migration guide in PR
- tara: finalize copy text for Preference labels and tooltip about "High Contrast" mode

kevin: I'll open the PR and add screenshots for mobile/tablet. Expect draft branch by EOD Friday.

tara: Also suggest we add a small "Preview contrast" tool in Appearance where you can toggle simulated colorblindness and reduced contrast to validate quickly.

maya: Love that. Will add to product backlog.

dinesh: Quick dev Q: should we allow per-team custom brand color (enterprise) and then auto-generate accessible variants? Feels tricky but nice to have.

maya: Let's scope that for Dedicated customers later. For now, we'll document constraints: brand hue must meet contrast and chart exclusion rules.

a11y-bot: Final check reminder: run axe-core on the prototype once figma tokens are finalized.

maya: Thanks all! leaving comments on figma now :sparkles:
